purpose: Explain the three active multi-country routes that actually include Kaieteur Falls, the aviation connection from Georgetown, guide-led park viewpoint visit, differences in travel days/included flights and weather contingencies, while separating the waterfall excursion from longer nature expeditions.

externalSources.supports: Official protected-area information: Kaieteur is on the Potaro River, approximately 226-meter free fall, national park founded in 1929 and expanded to more than 60,000 hectares.
Protected landscape and cultural significance to the Patamona people, rainforest and plateau habitats.
Visitor access to Kaieteur is managed through permitted park tours and applicable safety requirements.

notes: Commercial content from exactly three active tour MD files, and all three include Kaieteur in their main routes.

Correct public waterfall height is approximately 226 m, supported by protected-area authorities and tour programs. An outdated destination body says 270 m and is not treated as reliable; no unrelated destination edit made.
Seven-day tour covers Guyana at the end, nine-/fourteen-day tours at start. Longer tours add time mostly in Suriname, not extra days inside Kaieteur National Park.
All three include round-trip Kaieteur excursion flights, but included Guyana–Suriname inter-country airfare differs by tour.
No guaranteed flight/animal sightings, invented park overnight, extra waterfall stop, fixed departure dates or unsupported booking availability. All article links internal.
